name: Engineering Capital
identity_check: Confirmed as Engineering Capital (engineeringcapital.com), the Bay Area seed firm Ashmeet Sidana founded in 2015, where he is 'Founder and Chief Engineer'; legal entity Engineering Capital, LLC (site footer). SEC EDGAR returns exactly five entities for the name, Engineering Capital Fund I-V, L.P., each Form D signed by Ashmeet S. Sidana as Managing Member of the General Partner. Their addresses move from Palo Alto (I, II) to Menlo Park (III) to 745 Burgoyne Street, Mountain View (IV, V), which is the registered address on the firm's contact page. Not engcapital.com, which is a parked domain for sale. Not the generic term 'engineering capital'. StartupIntros mixes unrelated deals (e.g. Moonvalley, Cognition, Pontera, SafelyYou) and a fintech focus into its profile of this name; those were not recorded.

thesis_text.value: Ashmeet Sidana's solo-GP seed fund aims to be the first, lead investor in software and IT-infrastructure startups built on a technical insight that a capable engineer could not build merely from being told what it is. Backs technical founders early, often before they start a company; favours capital-efficient software over hardware. Recent bets skew to AI, security and developer tools.

open_items: Check size: the only stated figure is $500K-$1M per investment (Global Venturing, Feb 2015, Fund I era). It is probably out of date for the $60-77M funds that followed; no current check size is published on the site or in press read.

No application form, email or pitch URL. The contact page says the best route is a mutual introduction; the essay's 'we will be happy to review your plan' links back to that page. accepts_cold_inbound = 'no' is inferred from this and could be 'unknown'.

requires_us_entity and investment in Indian founders are not stated anywhere read. Sidana appears on India-focused podcasts (100x Entrepreneur, The Neon Show), and Neon Fund co-invested in Guickly, but there is no stated policy.
portfolio_count_reported: no number is stated. The homepage shows about 42 linked current portfolio logos and 21 'Previous Investments' (counted, not stated).

Fund close_dates are the Form D filing dates that report each offering as fully sold, not announced final-close dates. Fund V's first sale was 2025-10-29. The homepage disclaimer still names only Funds I-IV, and the site footer reads 2015-2024.
The WSJ 2015 fund article (the lead link, now wsj.com/articles/BL-VCDB-16496) is paywalled (HTTP 401) and was not read. Fund I is confirmed by Form D, StrictlyVC and Global Venturing instead.

Rounds that StartupIntros attributes to Engineering Capital but that could not be confirmed on a readable page naming the firm (Business Wire returned 403): Tidalwave Series A ($22M, Nov 2025), WideField Security Series A ($11.3M, Oct 2025; Cisco completed its acquisition of WideField on 2026-07-31), Trustero Series A ($10M, Nov 2024) and Scoop Analytics seed (Mar 2025). TechCrunch's CodeRabbit Series B ($60M, 2025-09-16) names only CRV among returning investors.

Industrial and supply-chain portfolio companies with no public round naming Engineering Capital found: Kipo AI (AI sourcing and procurement agents, BOM risk scrubbing), Elm AI (supply-chain procurement and supplier-risk agents), Kahuna Labs (the site renders only via JavaScript) and Cloudexe (GPU pooling; its site lists Engineering Capital as investor). Tignis (AI process control for manufacturing) was later acquired by Cohu; the Cohu release returned 403.

Tignis 2019: GeekWire names 'Ashmeet Sidana of Engineering Capital' as an investor (he also sat on Tignis' advisory board), so it is unclear whether the check came from the fund or from Sidana personally.

Partners: Sidana is the only investing partner (solo GP). Adina Luo (part-time operations) and the mentors Jim Anderson, Steve Blank, Scott Bonham and George Kadifa are not recorded as partners. The firm's site links Sidana's X account, not a LinkedIn profile.

Fit note: the firm's own essay says a hardware technical insight is less valuable to startups and that it favours capital-efficient software. Its Phase 1 category (industrial / hard tech / physical AI) does not match its stated thesis.
Web search budget ran out mid-research, so further 2025-2026 rounds may exist that this file does not cover.
